prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports: Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport (keep safety authority). Elements: Demand Prediction Service (DPS, Marlinstone; unconstrained demand; AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM); Slot Allocation Engine (SAE, Blueharbor; regulated demand, CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time); Departure Metering Service (DMS, Emberline; weights sequencing by Passenger Misconnect Count when connection protection approved). DPS/CAM/SAE/DMS reject data lacking trusted timestamp from Time Synchronization Service. Airport CDM Portal; Identity Access Service (IAS); Audit Event Ledger (AEL); Alert Distribution Hub (urgent discrepancies, Digital Briefing Room); Performance Analytics Warehouse (PAW; role-limited; data quality measures; delay absorption = DPS vs SAE vs Flight Data Exchange realized times, minutes at origin/arrival stream/surface; queue and slot adherence metrics); Collaborative Decision Log; Business Rules Registry (BRR; thresholds, reason codes, mode exceptions, tolerance windows); Tower Sequence Manager (milestones, runway sequence counts); Ramp Movement Board (milestones, surface queue counts); North/South Runway Meter, East/West Apron Sensor (independent queue checks); Surface Surveillance Adapter; Weather Ingest Gateway (Meteorology Briefing Officer); Flight Data Exchange (validates Flight Intent Message, realized times); Airline Interface Adapter; Handling Resource Planner; Common Situation Display (freshness: current/aging/stale/unavailable); Contingency Operations Console; North/South Runway. Silverpine SHALL accept emergency access only after IAS records incident reference/expiry. Actors: Airline Operations Coordinator (TOBT=Target Off Block Time updates; frozen at horizon, changes need reason code); Regional Flow Manager (RFM; verifies Ground Delay Program via delay absorption); Slot Coordinator (reviews adherence vs CTT/TOBT by operator/airport/time band/regulation); Data Governance Steward (discrepancies: mark disputed, keep prior value; ownership register; stewardship reviews); System Support Engineer; Airport Duty Manager. Validation: schema, mandatory, code set, temporal, plausibility. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode; Capacity Reduction State; Recovery Phase; Slot Compliance State (adherence priority over optimization); Contingency Fallback State (ADM declares after consulting RFM). Daily repeatable indicators required.

New part:
S852: Cancellation avoidance shall be estimated by comparing actual cancellations with a baseline scenario derived from demand, capacity, weather, and historical disruption outcomes.
S853: The Capacity Assessment Module shall record the available Airport Acceptance Rate used in each baseline so that avoided cancellation estimates remain traceable.
S854: The Airline Operations Coordinator and Aircraft Operator Representative shall be able to challenge cancellation avoidance results through the Collaborative Decision Log when local business decisions affected the outcome.
S855: Emissions reduction shall be estimated from reduced airborne holding, reduced taxi-out time, avoided engine running in queues, and smoother departure metering.
S856: The Performance Analytics Warehouse shall apply approved fuel burn and emissions factors by aircraft category, operating phase, and delay location.
S857: Emissions metrics shall distinguish between actual reductions and delay transfers that only move fuel burn from one phase of flight to another.
S858: The Meteorology Briefing Officer shall support interpretation of emissions results by identifying periods when weather routing or convective avoidance dominated fuel performance.
S859: Stakeholder benefit tracking shall allocate measured outcomes to aircraft operators, airport operations, air navigation service functions, ground handling activities, and passengers where the source data supports that attribution.
S860: The Airport Duty Manager shall receive benefit summaries that show changes in stand occupancy, surface congestion, recovery duration, and passenger-facing disruption indicators.
S861: The Data Governance Steward shall ensure that published performance measures identify data sources, calculation versions, confidence limits, and known exclusions.
S862: The Post Operations Report shall present regional benefits alongside operational trade-offs so that decision makers can see whether delay, queue, slot, cancellation, and emissions objectives were balanced in practice.
S863: Training for the Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System shall be role based and shall cover normal coordination, constrained operations, recovery actions, and degraded system use.
S864: The Regional Flow Manager shall receive advanced instruction on interpreting demand and capacity information, leading collaborative decisions, and authorizing operational measures in the Regional Flow Platform.
S865: Air traffic controllers shall be trained to understand how flow measures, sequencing changes, and calculated times affect sector workload, runway demand, and controller tactical flexibility.
S866: The Tower Supervisor shall receive practical training on the Tower Sequence Manager, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, North Runway Meter, and South Runway Meter.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
